fields.title: Perceived speed
fields.keyTakeaway: Speed perception is built on instant feedback, showing progress, appearance order, and the absence of layout shifts, and it is cheaper to improve than actual time.
fields.sections/0/blocks/0/text: Two screens load in 1.5 seconds. Why does one feel fast and the other slow?
fields.sections/1/blocks/0/text: Perception determines user behavior, not measured time. A product can gain more in feel than in milliseconds, and this is usually cheaper than optimization.
fields.sections/2/blocks/0/text: [[perceived-performance|Speed perception]] is determined by four things besides actual time.
fields.sections/2/blocks/1/text: **Immediate reaction to action.** A tap must give feedback within 100 ms—highlight, animation, state change. Without this, the user is unsure if they tapped and taps again.
fields.sections/2/blocks/2/text: **Progress instead of emptiness.** A [[skeleton-screen|skeleton screen]]—outlines of future content—is perceived as faster than a spinner for the same duration. It shows what is loading and creates a sense that progress is being made.
fields.sections/2/blocks/3/text: **Order of appearance.** First what matters: text before images, the first screen before the rest. The person starts reading while the rest loads and does not notice the difference.
fields.sections/2/blocks/4/text: **Absence of shifts.** Content that appears and shifts what is already shown destroys the feeling of readiness more than an extra second of waiting.
fields.sections/2/blocks/5/text: Separately—[[optimistic-ui|optimistic actions]] from `IN1-N4-L2`: the result is shown before server confirmation. A feeling of instant response with unchanged actual time.
fields.sections/2/blocks/6/text: Practical ratio: **improving perception usually takes days, improving actual time takes weeks.** It is sensible to start with the former.
fields.sections/3/blocks/0/text: Three changes without a single millisecond of metric gains:
fields.sections/3/blocks/1/text: *Skeleton instead of spinner* on the main screen. Pre-load drop-off fell from 8% to 5.5%.
fields.sections/3/blocks/2/text: *Rendering order:* text and price cards first, images fading in later. The user starts choosing sooner.
fields.sections/3/blocks/3/text: *Reserving space for images.* Previously cards shifted when images loaded, and people missed buttons. The "app jumps" complaint disappeared.
fields.sections/3/blocks/4/text: Separately on feedback: the add-to-cart button used to show state change after the server response, 240 ms. Moved to the client, feedback became instant. The number of repeat taps dropped by 60%—which means fewer cart duplicates and support tickets.
fields.sections/4/blocks/0/text: Perception does not replace speed. A skeleton shown for eight seconds does not help—it makes it obvious that nothing is happening.
fields.sections/5/blocks/0/text: Speed perception is built on instant feedback, showing progress, appearance order, and the absence of layout shifts, and it is cheaper to improve than actual time.
